items.detail: The same definition, instance, operation and arguments give the same Decision and the same serialized bytes.
items.label: Deterministic decisions

items.detail: entity-core reads no clock, filesystem, network, environment or random source and depends only on serde and serde_json.
items.label: No IO in the kernel

items.detail: A refused operation leaves the caller's instance untouched and produces no events.
items.label: A refusal changes nothing

items.detail: A misspelled key, an unknown condition operator or a condition with two operators is refused, not ignored.
items.label: Closed definition documents

items.detail: A comparison over a value nobody observed answers unknown, and the refusal names every missing path.
items.label: Three-valued rules

items.detail: An object with several broken values reports every error, each with its path.
items.label: Accumulated validation

items.detail: starts_with and ends_with compare bytes, case-sensitively, under every semantics (0.24.0).
items.label: Prefix and suffix conditions

items.detail: A set value written as increment: n adds n to a required integer or number field inside the decision, exactly, and a sum the field's kind cannot hold is refused rather than wrapped.
items.label: Increment assignments

items.detail: A ref field names another entity type; validate_all refuses a reference to a type nobody registered.
items.label: Typed references

items.detail: Operations and creations carry ordered branches with guards, effects, responses and declared refusals; the kernel selects the branch.
items.label: Named outcomes (service/1)

items.detail: A copied optional argument stays absent, present or null through replay and retry.
items.label: Optional values keep their absence (service/2)

items.detail: Set, Preserve and Remove actions apply after the outcome is selected and are kept in the record.
items.label: Typed update actions (service/3)

items.detail: A service definition may declare an identity field; derived creation computes the storage address from it.
items.label: Logical identity and derived addresses

items.detail: A service rule reads the length of a declared string as path.count, counted in Unicode scalar values with no normalization (0.27.0).
items.label: Text length in service rules

items.detail: A service string field or argument may declare an alphabet; a value outside it is a validation error naming the first offending character, and generated contracts carry it as x-alphabet (0.27.0).
items.label: Text alphabets

items.detail: replay re-executes a complete decision record and refuses a record whose result was altered.
items.label: Verified decision replay

items.detail: rehydrate folds an event-only history and refuses an event no operation emits on its transition.
items.label: Legacy event folding

items.detail: One black-box suite holds Memory and File stores to the same write contract.
items.label: Provider conformance suites

items.detail: entity store migrate-file copies a pre-0.15 store out of place; --dry-run writes nothing.
items.label: File Store v2 and its migration

items.detail: State, history and events commit in one SQLite transaction.
items.label: SQLite provider

items.detail: The same contract against a server the caller connects to; the gate runs it only when ENTITY_POSTGRES_URL is set.
items.label: PostgreSQL provider

items.detail: A store behind a caller-provided transport; a server that did not answer is Unreachable, never Absent.
items.label: Remote protocol

items.detail: Authority, read path, offline and divergence behaviour are declared; divergences replay later with catch_up.
items.label: Hybrid authority and catch-up

items.detail: entity-query pages one entity type by JSON containment; a cursor is bound to the query that issued it.
items.label: Document queries

items.detail: entity-executor runs complete recorded commands over async storage ports; a retry returns the original result.
items.label: Asynchronous executor with exact retries

items.detail: execute_versioned and batch_versioned decide on a version the caller names (0.26.0).
items.label: Explicit definition versions

items.detail: entity-eventlog keeps complete records on Eventlog file, sqlite, postgres and tree providers, provisioned explicitly before an open.
items.label: Eventlog providers

items.detail: On a tree store two branches that both decided for one subject fork it; BatchAction::Merge joins the heads.
items.label: Forked subjects and merge

items.detail: An executor built with recording_refusals records each refusal once and moves no subject.
items.label: Recorded refusals

items.detail: import_anchors establishes a batch of imported boundaries in one append group, and a retry of it settles.
items.label: Batch import of legacy histories

items.detail: A new tree store is eventlog-tree/2; an eventlog-tree/1 store reads the same after migration (0.25.0).
items.label: Tree stores keep each text once

items.detail: CapturePolicy::ProviderTracked reuses a verified observation SQLite proves unchanged (0.26.0); held to its own executable contract.
items.label: Provider-tracked reads on SQLite

items.detail: With durable open checkpoints enabled, a ProviderTracked open verifies the persisted checkpoint and the appends since it, not the whole history.
items.label: Open from a persisted checkpoint on SQLite

items.detail: Validate, inspect, graph, create, execute, list and store migrations from one Rust binary with typed exit codes.
items.label: The entity command

items.detail: A build with the eventlog-providers feature provisions and uses an Eventlog File store; no gate step builds that feature.
items.label: Eventlog File through the command

items.detail: Text, Mermaid, DOT, SVG and HTML, the same bytes on every run.
items.label: Lifecycle and reference graphs

items.detail: entity generate docs writes a static bundle and replaces only a directory it generated.
items.label: Entity pages, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI

items.detail: Schema-derived create, get, list, events and operation tools; a stale call is refused and changes nothing.
items.label: MCP tools over stdio

items.detail: entity generate rust-cli compiles a command with one subcommand per entity and operation.
items.label: Definition-specific Rust CLI

items.detail: entity skill renders a version-stamped Agent Skills document; replacing a file needs --force.
items.label: Agent skill

items.detail: entity-core, entity-store, entity-executor, entity-shell and entity-query are checked against their ESS scenarios by the gate.
items.label: Executable ESS contracts for five libraries

items.detail: A schema generated from the Rust definition types.
items.label: JSON Schema for the definition format

items.detail: Moving stored instances from one definition version to another.
items.label: Definition migrations

items.detail: Why an operation is or is not permitted from the current state.
items.label: entity explain

items.detail: Reusable named rules, reusable schema fragments and definition inheritance.
items.label: Named predicates and schema fragments

items.detail: A service response checked against its declared fields, including alphabet and max_length.
items.label: Responses checked against their schema

items.detail: A service/1 outcome with a moves effect loads through entity-yaml and the entity command.
items.label: Moves outcomes in YAML

items.detail: Registered definitions served as an HTTP and a NATS interface; today OpenAPI and AsyncAPI are contracts only.
items.label: Definitions served over HTTP and NATS
